notes.title: Small tools. Long life.
notes.summary: A useful program should still make sense when you come back to it next year.
paragraphs: The tools I keep coming back to have a few things in common: a clear job, readable source, and a way to take my data with me. They do not need a subscription to remain useful.

That is the direction of this workshop. PHP for a small web interface, SQLite when a single file is enough, Python for a practical command-line task, and Go when a portable executable makes the job easier. The language follows the problem.
Simple does not mean careless. Validation, clear failure messages, a tested restore process, and useful documentation matter more than a complicated architecture.
CoolCode is where the runnable projects live. This site is the notebook beside the workbench: the questions, experiments, and decisions that connect them.

notes.title: A home for local DNS.
notes.summary: Local names and reverse lookups belong close to the machines they describe.
paragraphs: A home network becomes easier to understand when its services have names. A resolver can answer the questions about the local network and forward the rest to an upstream service.

The design I am exploring pairs dnsmasq for local records with an encrypted upstream resolver. The home.arpa namespace gives local names a clear boundary. Reverse lookups should be answered locally too.

The next useful layer is an inventory: when a device last appeared, which address it used, and what services it advertised. Discovery and publication should be separate steps, so an observed device does not automatically become a trusted DNS entry.
The goal is a network I can explain, export, and repair. A dashboard is useful only if the underlying records remain understandable.

notes.title: An archive is only useful if it opens.
notes.summary: Keeping the bytes is the beginning. Finding and reading them is the next job.
paragraphs: A directory of saved files is a good start. An archive becomes much more useful when it also preserves context: what a file is, where it came from, and how to open it.

Archive Shelf approaches the finding problem with full-text search and links back to original pages. Waystation approaches the disappearing-website problem with portable captures. Tape Index helps check whether the bytes still match a saved manifest.
These are different parts of the same habit: keep originals, make searchable derivatives, and keep enough information to reproduce the process.
I prefer an archive that remains usable without the software that created it. Plain text, conventional files, and documented exports make that a realistic goal.

ideas.title: Portfolio notebook
ideas.label: IBKR API / PERSONAL DASHBOARD
ideas.summary: A private place to understand positions, cash, and changes over time.
ideas.first_step: Start with a read-only view of one account’s positions, plus a local snapshot and a simple comparison against the previous snapshot.
ideas.questions: Choose the appropriate IBKR API and confirm account permissions, authentication, and data entitlements. Keep credentials server-side. The concept has no order-entry flow.

ideas.title: The long-way ride journal
ideas.label: STRAVA API / RIDES & EXPLORATION
ideas.summary: Connect rides with notes about the places, detours, and photographs worth remembering.
ideas.first_step: Prototype a private ride list for the connected athlete, with distance, date, and manually written field notes.
ideas.questions: Check Strava’s current access, subscription, display, and retention requirements before building. Keep exact routes and start/end locations private by default.

ideas.title: Small signals
ideas.label: ESP32 / MQTT / HOME LAB
ideas.summary: A small sensor project with a dashboard that makes its readings useful.
ideas.first_step: Try a low-voltage room sensor and a local MQTT topic. Save a simple history and display when the last reading arrived.
ideas.questions: Pick one useful measurement, decide how long to keep it, and show missing or stale data clearly. A desk display could be a later extension.

ideas.title: Contact sheet
ideas.label: PHOTOGRAPHY / PRIVATE ARCHIVES
ideas.summary: Find the photograph you remember by its light, mood, or subject.
ideas.first_step: Generate thumbnails from a small folder of copied images, add manual tags, and produce a portable contact sheet.
ideas.questions: Preserve originals and keep derivatives separate. Decide which metadata is useful privately and strip location data from public exports.
